notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in
it counts as correct for this topic_id, with the first entry the
primary answer and later ones tolerated alternatives. evaluate.py
still records the exact verdict produced for the confusion matrix
-- this list only controls what counts as correct.
For representation-only requirements (tax liability, felony
conviction, SAM registration), 'compliant' means the application
text contains the required self-representation, correctly
completed -- not that the underlying fact was independently
verified. No text-only tool can confirm a live SAM registration or
an IRS record; that is outside this pipeline's scope.
A null acceptable_verdicts marks a topic this file does not score
for verdict accuracy. Currently only submission_deadline_and_channel,
since it is is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json and
never gets a verdict from a correctly-behaving pipeline.
prior_experience_count and prior_experience_poc_required are
separate topics: the application names three references, two with
full descriptions and complete points of contact, one with only a
vague description and no point of contact.
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in
true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone;
true_requirements.json is the source of truth if the two diverge.

amendment_acknowledgment_if_posted broadened to also accept non_compliant after a real pipeline run: the application includes an explicit 'documents included in this quote package' checklist that omits signed amendments/SF30 acknowledgments, and the model reasonably read that enumerated omission as closer to affirmative evidence than plain silence would be.

primary_verdict / primary_verdict_source (added by SFT data-prep pass): a single training-target label per topic, additive -- acceptable_verdicts is unchanged and remains the source of truth for verdict-accuracy scoring. primary_verdict is the pipeline's own correct prediction where one exists (source: pipeline_prediction), else acceptable_verdicts[0] (source: acceptable_verdicts_first). null for topics with acceptable_verdicts: null (excluded from SFT training, same as they're excluded from verdict scoring).

verdicts.description: Must be a small business under NAICS 238990 with a size standard of $19M average annual revenue.
verdicts.rationale: Application states average annual revenue as $12.4M in the Capabilities Statement and as $21.8M in Financial and Bonding Information for the same size-standard purpose -- directly conflicting figures for the same field. This is the deterministic numeric_threshold test case: extract_values should surface both numbers for the same field_name, and compare_condition should return CONTRADICTORY before any language-model verdict call happens. non_compliant is also acceptable (not ideal) because the second figure alone independently fails the $19M threshold, so a pipeline that misses the internal inconsistency but still correctly fails the requirement has not made the dangerous mistake -- compliant is the only unacceptable answer here.

average annual gross revenue of $12.4
million over the past three fiscal years

average annual revenue for size-standard purposes was $21.8
million

verdicts.description: The Price Schedule template must not be edited except to add units of measure/quantities; if changes are needed, an addendum explaining them must be provided alongside the unedited schedule.
verdicts.rationale: The application shows a filled-in price schedule (item, price, total) but never represents, one way or the other, whether the underlying template itself was left unedited. Nothing in application.txt lets a text-only check confirm or deny this, so insufficient_information is the only defensible call -- compliant would be false confidence, non_compliant would be an unjustified accusation.

verdicts.description: Must provide at least 3 prior experience references for projects similar in size and scope, completed within the past 5 years.
verdicts.rationale: Three distinct engagements are named, satisfying the count. The third is described only in general terms ('various municipal handrail and railing projects... over the years') without a specific project or contract value, which is a defensible basis for either a clean compliant call or a more cautious insufficient_information call about whether it truly matches the 'similar size and scope' bar -- non_compliant would be wrong, since three references genuinely are present.

verdicts.description: Each prior experience reference must include a project description and point-of-contact information.
verdicts.rationale: References 1 and 2 both include complete point-of-contact information. Reference 3 gives no point of contact at all, so the requirement's explicit 'contact information SHALL be provided' is unmet for that entry. non_compliant is the more precise call (a clear violation for one of three references); insufficient_information is also acceptable if the pipeline treats partial fulfillment as unable to confirm rather than as a clean fail. compliant is unacceptable -- it would miss a verifiable, unambiguous gap.

verdicts.description: If SAM.gov shows a posted amendment, the offeror must acknowledge it by signing the SF30 and provide it with the final quote/proposal package.
verdicts.rationale: The application includes an explicit checklist of documents included in the quote package (Checklist, Price Schedule, Capabilities Statement, Prior Experience References, Contractor Core Data) that omits any signed amendment/SF30 acknowledgment. Since the requirement is conditional (is_mandatory: false, applies only 'in any case an amendment was posted'), this enumerated omission is closer to affirmative evidence than plain silence would be -- a reasonable basis for non_compliant -- but the checklist alone does not confirm whether an amendment was actually posted, so compliant (nothing applicable) and insufficient_information (cannot tell) remain defensible too.

References, and Contractor Core Data.

verdicts.description: Must submit all required documents via email so as to reach the government office by the specified deadline; late submissions will not be accepted.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false -- this is about the process of submission (channel and timing), which application.txt (a capabilities-statement-style document) has no natural way to represent one way or the other. Deliberately not scored for verdict accuracy: the interesting failure mode here is the pipeline wrongly marking this is_text_verifiable: true and then guessing a verdict from silence, which the is_text_verifiable accuracy metric in true_requirements.json catches directly.
